title: At least that
html_source: At the beginning of Ulysses, Haines had suggested “Hamlet” was, by a theological reading, about the Son striving to be atoned with the Father (18). The suggestion has been applied to Ulysses (along with various others) in a more or less secular way, that the novel is about Stephen Dedalus meeting Leopold Bloom who is in need of a son in much the same way Stephen is in need of a father– and it is, it all very neatly corresponds to the Homeric frame. In Proteus, one can see a second thread which can be understood more broadly as a purpose of the novel, that the male consciousness is moving toward mother consciousness. Stephen’s desire for the mother is based in his need as a male, and especially as an artist, of anima or what has been called mother consciousness. A problem is that he continuously encounters the death-mother.
